title: Lesson 16 - When Model Access Is Withdrawn: Admin Controls, Author Impact, and Existing Templates
description: Explain how to manage and prevent specific models from being accessed.

questions.question: In what order does Agentforce determine which model a subagent uses?
options: The org default, then the agent, then the subagent
The subagent, then the agent, then the model selected in Setup
The prompt template, then the subagent, then the org default
questions.explanation: Agentforce checks the subagent model first, then the agent model, then the model selected in Setup, so a subagent override beats an agent override, which beats the org default.

questions.question: An author opens a prompt template that points at a model the admin just hid. What do they see and can the template still run?
options: The template is blocked until the model is shown again
The model runs but silently switches to the org default
The model is shown as hidden and the template runs the same as before
questions.explanation: A hidden model does not stop a template that already uses it; those templates run as before, and the author sees the model marked hidden and non-selectable rather than an error.

questions.question: A subagent uses a model override, and an action in that agent runs a prompt template. Which model does the prompt template use?
options: The model configured on the prompt template itself, which model override does not change
Always the org default, ignoring the template
questions.explanation: Model override does not affect the model that prompt templates in actions use, so the template runs on its own configured model regardless of the subagent or agent override.
